findings: March2011 (*PTS) explicitly applies to geometrically pro-Sigma arithmetic quotients with a non-p prime ell and asserts bijectivity for ell-cyclotomically full k. May2011 (*val) supplies section-fixed compatible valuations in the same restricted tower, so that interface is primary-paid.

For finite k/Qp and ell!=p, cyclotomic image is generated topologically by residue cardinality q. A positive integer q>1 is not an ell-adic root of unity; a suitable finite power has nonzero ell-adic logarithm, so its generated subgroup is open.

ABBR Cor6.21 uniquely lifts residue isomorphisms to local star covers. 7.4(2) identifies the automorphism group with the stabilizer of gluing data, not all metrized-complex automorphisms. The candidate must exhibit fixed gluing data.

For the oriented source circuit, residue Kummer orders +1 and -1 produce inverse characters at opposite ends. Inverse annular coordinates can intertwine these characters; free edge orbits admit gluing by transport. The no-loop hypothesis of7.4 must be handled by equivariant subdivision as in7.7. This is a proposed checked interface, not certification of the complete assembled theorem.

Source06 treats arbitrary finite Galois extensions, using roots of order m_b and normal closures of horizontal-index-ell covers. A pro-Sigma adaptation must retain Sigma-order normal closures at every auxiliary cover, compositum, patching component and first-stage realization; merely bounding cover degree is insufficient.
